summary: Intro demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints. Covered architecture, latency vs cost tradeoffs, typical routing and fallback patterns, and next steps for a pilot including benchmark plans and security artifacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Rivera: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Connor from the SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya Desai: Good, thanks. Excited to dig in, we want to get a concrete sense of how your hosted flow would work for our retail search use case.
[00:15] Connor Blake: Great. Quick agenda: we'll show the embeddings endpoint, how to do a similarity search, then the reranker endpoint and how to tie those together with the Console and Optimize suggestions. We'll leave time for Q&A and next steps.
[00:28] Tom Nguyen: Sounds good. We're especially sensitive to latency — sub 100ms tail ideally for our storefront. Also curious how you reduce token costs.
[00:38] Connor: Yep, we'll cover batching, prefix caching, and how model variants affect cost/latency.
[00:45] [00:45] Speaker 1 (auto): noise background
[00:50] Maya: Quick background, Helion said you're running a hybrid ES + vector store proto, correct?
[00:56] Priya: Right now ES for metadata, Pinecone for vectors in the POC. Looking to consolidate and reduce infra and costs. Also need SOC 2 and SSO support for enterprise.
[01:10] Connor: Redwood hosted API has embeddings and a dedicated rerank endpoint. Typical pattern: embed query, retrieve top N from vector DB, then call rerank to reorder by a learned cross-encoder. That gives better precision than pure dot-product.
[01:30] Sara Kim: How do you host the reranker? Is it a separate model or part of the same API?
[01:35] Connor: Good question. It's a separate endpoint. For hosted we run a cross-encoder optimized for latency: quantized weights, custom kernels. You can pick the model family — tradeoffs between quality and inference time.
[01:48] [01:48] Tom: And caching? If a lot of catalog queries are repeated, can you cache results?
[01:52] Connor: Yes — we have automatic prefix/KV cache on the runtime for reranker K/V and on retrieval layer caching suggestions in Console. For high hit-rate queries that massively cuts per-request tokens and latency.
[02:05] Priya: Walk me through a real request flow — sample request/response.
[02:10] Connor: (shares screen) Here's the embeddings API call — POST /v1/embeddings with model param like redwood-emb-002, payload text, returns vector. Then you run nearest-neighbor locally or via your vector DB. Then POST /v1/rerank with candidate docs and the query, and you get scores. Example code snippet in Python.
[02:30] [02:30] Connor: code: 
client.embeddings.create(input=[query], model="redwood-emb-002")
# use faiss/pinecone to fetch top 50
client.rerank.create(model="redwood-rank-1", query=query, candidates=candidates)
[02:50] Sara: The reranker call — how big are the payloads? If we send 50 docs with full text, that's a lot of tokens.
[02:58] Connor: We usually pass short context snippets and IDs. Also there's chunking and truncation heuristics. For large docs we recommend precomputing summary snippets to pass to reranker. That reduces token usage.
[03:12] [03:12] Priya: Any built-in evaluation tools? We want to measure drift and quality across rollouts.
[03:18] Maya: Yes, Console has an evals tab. You can upload labeled queries and compare model variants — Redwood Optimize also suggests quantization profiles and batching configs based on your workload.
[03:30] [03:30] Tom: Cost math — can you give ballpark numbers for embeddings + rerank per 1M queries?
[03:36] Maya: Ballpark depends on model choice and hit rates. For our mid-tier emb model and lightweight reranker, we typically see unit cost dominated by rerank when candidates >16. Connor: If you cache aggressively and reduce candidate size it drops quickly. We'll include a cost example in the follow-up spreadsheet.
[03:55] [03:55] Priya: Security — do you maintain customer logs? What's retention?
[03:59] Connor: Hosted customers can opt into short retention for logs; enterprise plans get audit logs, KMS integration for encryption at rest, and VPC peering options. We have SOC 2 and ISO details in the security pack. We'll share that.
[04:15] [04:15] Speaker 2: (mumble)
[04:20] Connor: Now demo time. I'll run a small flow with Helion sample dataset we preloaded into a temp index.
[04:25] [04:25] Connor: (typing) Query: "women's black running shoes size 9 cushioned" — embeddings call returns vector in 30-40ms, then retrieval (local FAISS) ~20ms, rerank call returned in ~75ms for top 20 candidates.
[04:42] Priya: Those numbers look promising. What's the p95?
[04:46] Connor: In this test p95 was ~120ms on our hosted cluster for the rerank call — depends on model. We can target lower by switching to a faster reranker variant and enabling batching.
[05:00] Tom: Batching — does that increase tail latency for single-user sessions?
[05:04] Connor: There is a tradeoff: batching groups requests which improves throughput and reduces cost per token but can add a small queuing delay. You can configure per-route SLOs: keep latency sensitive routes unbatched or small windows.
[05:16] [05:16] Maya: Where does model routing come in? If your primary model is busy, can Redwood fallback to a cheaper variant?
[05:22] Connor: Exactly. Smart routing lets you set policies: prefer low-latency variants for checkout pages, fallback to cost-efficient variants for search. Canary rollouts are supported too.
[05:32] [05:32] Sara: About embeddings drift — we retrain indexing weekly. Does Redwood help surface regressions?
[05:37] Maya: Optimize watches your eval sets and emits alerts on quality regressions tied to prompt sets. It's part of the Optimize product. We can wire alerts to Slack or PagerDuty.
[05:49] [05:49] Tom: If we wanted private deployment later, how much changes for our devs?
[05:54] Connor: API contract remains the same. Private gives you a control plane in your VPC, keys in your KMS, and optional on-prem workers. Migration is mostly ops work, not dev.
[06:08] [06:08] Priya: ACLs — can we have role-based access and SSO?
[06:12] Maya: Yes, RBAC and SAML SSO supported on enterprise plans.
[06:16] [06:16] Priya: Any customers in retail with similar scale?
[06:19] Maya: We have a few. I'll share anonymized perf summaries.
[06:25] [06:25] Connor: Next I'll show Console: per-route latency, token breakdown, cache hit rate visuals, and Optimize suggestions. (shares screen) Here you can see token-level cost, trailing latency spikes, and per-model dashboards.
[06:42] Tom: Nice. Can we plug in our collector/observability?
[06:45] Connor: Yes, we support trace hooks and export to Datadog/New Relic, plus webhooks for alerts.
[06:52] [06:52] Sara: About reranker accuracy — can we train custom rerankers with our labels?
[06:56] Connor: We do model onboarding for custom fine-tuning in Professional/Enterprise tiers. For hosted small pilots we recommend pairwise rerankers with in-application labels and Optimize to tune thresholds.
[07:10] [07:10] Priya: Do you support embeddings for multi-lingual catalogs?
[07:13] Connor: Yes, there are multilingual embeddings. We'll point out recommended models for Asian markets; latency profiles vary.
[07:22] [07:22] Maya: Quick pause — any blockers on your side for a pilot?
[07:26] Priya: Need security docs, pricing, and a realistic perf test we can run. Also timeline: we'd like a pilot in April.
[07:35] Maya: That aligns — we can get the trial ready and Connor can run the benchmark with your sample data.
[07:40] [07:40] Tom: How much of the rerank cost is proportional to candidate size vs model size?
[07:45] Connor: Roughly linear with token count; more candidates = more tokens. Model compute matters for latency; a bigger cross-encoder increases per-token compute. We'll provide a sensitivity table.
[08:00] [08:00] Speaker 3: (brief echo)
[08:04] Connor: I'll also show the simple endpoint configuration you can paste into your service. Example config: route /search -> embeddings + retrieval microservice + rerank route, with policy: max_candidates 20, rerank_model redwood-rank-1, cache TTL 5m.
[08:23] Priya: TTL 5m might be low for product pages; how do you tune cache invalidation for frequent SKU updates?
[08:29] Connor: You can invalidate by SKU change events; Console exposes cache controls and APIs to purge keys. For catalogs with frequent price updates we recommend event-driven invalidation.
[08:44] [08:44] Maya: Pricing for hosted pilot — we typically offer trial credits and an overage sheet. We'll send that.
[08:50] Priya: Good. On governance: what logs do we get for GDPR requests?
[08:54] Connor: We can supply audit logs and per-request metadata to help with subject access requests. Data residency options exist for EMEA.
[09:05] [09:05] Sara: For the benchmark notebook — what metrics should we collect?
[09:08] Connor: Precision@k, MRR, latency p50/p95/p99, cost per query, and cache hit rate. We'll share a template with scripts to compute those.
[09:18] [09:18] Priya: Can we do an A/B between our current pipeline and Redwood rerank for 2 weeks?
[09:23] Maya: Absolutely. We support A/B rollouts in Console, route split by percentage. We can help set that up.
[09:32] [09:32] Tom: Any special networking for hosted?
[09:35] Connor: No mandatory peering, but you can set up VPC peering for lower latency and private traffic. For most pilots token-auth over TLS is fine.
[09:46] [09:46] Priya: Great — could you also include best practices for summarizing large docs to feed reranker?
[09:52] Connor: Yes — we'll include a short doc. The idea is to precompute a 40–80 token snippet per chunk focusing on user intent.
[09:59] [09:59] Maya: Okay let's open Q&A.
[10:02] [10:02] Tom: What's the SLA for hosted inference?
[10:05] Maya: For hosted we have a standard uptime SLA for paid tiers; dedicated/reserved offers stronger latency commitments. We'll put exact numbers in the follow-up.
[10:14] [10:14] Sara: Are there native integrations for Pinecone/FAISS/Weaviate?
[10:18] Connor: We provide adapters and examples for all; you can keep your current DB and just use our rerank API.
[10:25] [10:25] Priya: If we want to reduce rerank calls by using a light-weight classifier first, does Redwood support that pipeline?
[10:31] Connor: Yes — you can route through a cheap filter model to short-circuit sure matches and only rerank the ambiguous set. Console supports configuring that flow.
[10:42] [10:42] Maya: Time check — about 20 minutes left. Any deeper topics to cover?
[10:47] Priya: Can we do a quick look at Optimize suggestions for our query distribution?
[10:51] Connor: I don't have your real logs here but will demo with synthetic distribution. (switches) Optimize recommends model X for high recall, Y for fast ranking, suggests 16 candidate default and caching TTLs.
[11:10] [11:10] Connor: It also suggests quantization profiles for the reranker that keep accuracy within 1-2% while reducing compute by ~40%.
[11:22] Tom: If we later want on-prem, does the rerank code differ?
[11:26] Connor: No, same binaries; packaging is different. You control networking and keys.
[11:31] [11:31] Priya: Ok, next steps recap?
[11:34] Maya: I'll send pricing, trial links, security pack. Connor will share benchmark notebook and perf checklist. You (Priya) will send sample data for pilot by April 2. We'll set a technical deep dive for early April.
[11:49] Priya: Sounds good.
[11:52] Maya: Anything else?
[11:54] Liam O'Rourke: Could you include an example of the rerank payload size and cost table?
[11:58] Connor: Yes — adding that to the follow-up.
[12:02] [12:02] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by end of this week.
[12:05] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[12:06] [12:06] call ended

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., model names mistyped, some speaker labels simplified). References: shared deck (link in chat), sample index preloaded for demo (temporary), follow-up spreadsheet with cost breakdown to be shared.
